ruling: Nothing is OP if everything is OP. Every card swings a fight on its own; the game is in the combos. A few classes are OP alone and are meant to be. The day’s roll, never a nerf, is what decides which OP is OP today.

philosophy.t: Common is a quarter more cook, Rare nearly half, Epic almost double. No augment is a rounding error; the first pick at midnight already changes how the fight looks.

Two cards that click on one cook, two cooks whose kits talk, two held augments that fuse, three pieces that make a Menu. The catalogue is written so that every card has at least two partners and the Prep screen shows them.
Every class has a House Combo: two of its own Signatures that turn its kit into a problem by itself. Some are louder than others and that is fine; the table has five seats.

Enemy numbers are cut against a table that runs two combos, not against a bare kit. Courses III and IV are thicker than in v1; the fresh midnight table still lands at six hundred because it holds one card and no combo.
Every Menu lists the day that breaks it. Today’s Service and the node modifiers are rolled, never picked, so the strongest build in the kitchen is the strongest build only on the days that let it be.

offerRules.t: HMD: one Pantry, one Facet, one Signature per window, always. OXP seats: two general, one gem.
Entries that click with, fuse with or complete a Menu with something you hold are 50% more likely. Held augments reappear at 20% so a card can be tiered.
By your fourth window at least one card on offer completes a Click you can make. Nothing else is guaranteed.
Taking a held augment again raises it one tier. Epic is the ceiling except through Recipes.
One free reroll a day in HMD; Lucky Spoon adds more. In OXP a reroll costs 15 gauge; Pantry Key widens offers instead.
They queue. A cook who opens the app at 20:00 picks four in a row at the tiers those windows had.
A Table combo takes one slot in the Special offer and is marked with both halves. A Menu card appears in the lobby once two of three are held.
Same tier pattern, same pools, same enemy roll for the whole city. The leaderboard compares choices, not luck of the hour.

borrow.idea: Personal, family and universal relic pools; relics amplify what a unit already does.

borrow.idea: Additive chips, multiplicative mult, and the joy of a chain that reads left to right.
borrow.lands: Clicks and Menus are the mult. Cards add; combos multiply; the Prep screen reads like a hand.

borrow.idea: Duo boons appear only when two gods are already in the run.
borrow.lands: Table combos: offered only when the table has the pair, for everyone at it.

borrow.idea: Two held items evolve into one stronger thing and the recipe is shown once you hold half.
borrow.lands: Recipes, shown from the first half, slot returned.

borrow.idea: Augments at fixed stages, a daily tier pattern shared by every player, three-piece traits that go online.
borrow.lands: Prep windows and OXP rows 1, 4, 7; the city’s shared pattern; Menus as the three-piece traits.

borrow.idea: Boss relics with a price, rarity floors by where you found them, melting relics, act blessings.
borrow.lands: Boss relics, node-weight floors, Leftover relics, Course blessings.

borrow.idea: Stacking the same item is the upgrade path and the enemy curve rises to meet it.
borrow.lands: Duplicates tier up; Courses III and IV are cut against a table with combos online.

builds.take: Long Burn, Wildfire, Flash Point for the Inferno Menu; Slow Roast for the Inferno Click; Special Open Flame.
builds.why: Burn becomes the horde’s own weapon: every death lights its neighbours at max stacks, and the cleave keeps the fire moving. The 999 that clears at 22:00 most often looks like this.

builds.take: Bulwark, Anchor, Cold Shoulder for Blizzard; Cast Iron + Hot Plate fusing to Cast-Iron Skin; Table combo The Wall.
builds.why: Two immovable fronts that Freeze everything that touches them, with thorns doing the killing. Slow honest kills and a table that reaches Course IV with nobody down.

builds.take: Compound, Green Thumb, Harvest for the Garden Menu; Share the Find, Full Basket; Table combo Picnic.
builds.why: Nothing happens for two hundred kills, then every Ingredient is a heal and every heal is a permanent stat. The table that is stronger at 2:30 than it was at the bell.

builds.take: Encore + Sharp Plating for Knife Work; Proof, Second Opinion, Table combo Precision for the Critic’s Menu.
builds.why: Marked enemies take +150% and every chained crit executes and jumps the mark. The Taster points, the Foodsmith finishes; Champions last four seconds.
builds.breaks: The Ghost of the Old Master, Double Booking.

builds.take: Chop Chop, Chain Reaction, Steady Hands for the Butcher’s Menu; Splash Zone for Cleaver; Pinch of Salt.
builds.why: The build for a cook who never saw a good Facet: crits execute half the field and carry three times over. Proof that the universal pool is a build on its own.

builds.take: Red Hand, Kindling, Fury on the seats; Kindling + Long Burn for Inferno on seat 1; Salt Cellar, Family Recipe for House Colours; Poison Ring after the Judge.
builds.why: R R R every turn at +25% mono, Sear permanent, no Trinity so Counter is paid in full: Anchor and Cast Iron on seat 2 keep the Nerve alive. Routes around Ashen.

builds.take: Opener, Closer for Bookends; Trinity Ring, Dinner Bell, Chef’s Whistle for the Trinity Menu; Round Table.
builds.why: Every Trinity buys two turns, skips Counter, refunds its token and keeps its buffs. The table that never sees the Colossus attack.

builds.take: Deep Ward + Ice Armour for Glacier Wall; Frost Wall; Regrowth on the Emerald for Cold Storage; Sous Vide after the Judge.
builds.why: Counter never reaches Nerve, blue buffs run long, and the Emerald’s kills refill everything. Scores on lives kept.

builds.take: Tip Jar, Michelin Star, Coin Purse for the Score Menu; Mise en Place + Opener for First Course on seat 1; Quick Fingers.
builds.why: The run that aims at the board, not the Colossus: every Starter monster dies on turn one for triple points, and the Elites are taken on purpose.

builds.take: Kindling on the Ruby, Harvest on an Emerald for Char Siu; Compound + Overgrowth for Old Growth; Full Course.
builds.why: Every Sear tick is a Grow stack and every stack regenerates Nerve. Weak in row one, absurd by row eight.

tuning.t: Common ≈ +25% of a cook’s output, Rare +45%, Epic +80%. A Click adds about half again on top of both halves; a Table combo about +60% for the cooks in it; a Recipe is two Epics and a free slot; a Menu changes the fight.
Partners pull at 50%; by the fourth window at least one card completes a Click you can make; Menus show at two of three.

Courses III and IV carry +30% HP and +20% ATK over v1 in data/hmd.json; OXP monster HP follows the TTK targets, so OXP absorbs the catalogue automatically. The fresh midnight target stays six hundred.

Every Menu lists the day that breaks it. The harness checks that every augment is top-quartile on some daily roll and bottom-quartile on another; a card that is never bottom-quartile is the one to look at.
Any five-augment build with no Click, Table combo or Recipe is flagged; fewer than 5% of evening builds should land there.
15–60% when offered. Flag above 75% or below 8%. Wide on purpose: a card people love is not a problem.
An augment still changes one thing so a hand reads cleanly; the multiplication lives in the combos, where it is named.
Sentence case, full stops, the real × and ·, no exclamation marks, and every name is something you could find in a kitchen.
